body:
Please leave your feedback about the new [mini.statuscolumn](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/readmes/mini-statuscolumn.html) module here. Feel free to either add new comment or positively upvote existing one.

Some things I am interested to find out (obviously, besides bugs):

- Does it work well out of the box?
- Is configuration intuitive enough?
- Are default values of settings convenient for you?
- Is documentation and examples clear enough?

Thanks!

comment_data.body: It's working perfectly but I could not get the same experience as the demo even though I enabled `number` and `cursorline` and set `signcolumn="yes"` and `foldcolumn="0"` as recommended by the demo video. This how my statuscolumn looks:

Out of the box it runs super smoothly and looks pretty good, plugged into [my config](https://code.rvx.works/RVxLab/rvx.nvim) it looks like this (active and inactive respectively) with signcolumn set to `yes` and `foldcolumn` unset (default to `0`): For me specifically this felt a bit too compact and I (currently) don't use folds. The docs were good at explaining on how to change that. I ended landing on the format `s=l=`, which looks like The wrap markers are a super nice addition here. Great work! ## Issue with `Snacks.terminal` One issue I found so far is that if you open a floating terminal through `Snacks.terminal` then the statuscolumn isn't properly undimmed when it's closed. I was able to reproduce that using `Snacks.lazygit` and my own Tuxedo plugin when Snacks is installed. ### Reproduction steps Config: ```lua vim.g.mapleader = " " vim.o.statuscolumn = "yes" vim.wo.cursorline = true vim.wo.number = true local with_snacks = vim.env.ENABLE_SNACKS ~= nil local packages = { "https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.statuscolumn", "https://github.com/RVxLab/tuxedo.nvim", } if with_snacks then table.insert(packages, "https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim") end vim.pack.add(packages) require("mini.statuscolumn").setup() require("tuxedo").setup() vim.keymap.set("n", "t", function () require("tuxedo").tuxedo() end) if with_snacks then require("snacks").setup() vim.keymap.set("n", "g", function () Snacks.lazygit.open() end) end ``` Requires [Tuxedo](https://github.com/webstonehq/tuxedo) to be installed locally. Steps: 1. Run Neovim without Snacks (omit `ENABLE_SNACKS` env var) 2. Install the plugins 3. Press `t` or run `:Tuxedo` 4. Press `q` 5. The statuscolumn is no longer dimmed 6. Exit Neovim 7. Run Neovim with Snacks (`ENABLE_SNACKS=1 nvim`) 8. Install Snacks 9. Press `g` and/or `t` 10. Press q on either window 11. The statuscolumn stays dimmed If you then repeat steps 1-5 you'll note that the statuscolumn acts like normal.

> This how my statuscolumn looks:

@AGN907, yes this is how it is supposed to look. The colored stuff is signs which are displayed to the right of line numbers. In the demo there are no signs (showing them would probably be a better idea), so the empty two cell column between line numbers and separator is for signs (since `signcolumn=yes` means to always show the column to reduce flickering).

---

For clarity, here is my reasoning for the default `lnum-sign-fold-sep` order:
- I do want a separator between column and buffer text, as it looks better (in my opinion) and serves as a clear delimiter between them. Using the regular vertical box drawing line (`│`) felt a bit cramped when there is a "bar" cursor at the line start (which happens frequently in Insert mode). After some experimentation I found that a left aligned vertical line (`▏`) is better suited here.
- Showing text to this left aligned vertical line feels cramped. So there needs to be some kind of whitespace there:
    - Forcing an "always on" whitespace (i.e. using ` ▏` as separator) feels like wasting horizontal space.
    - Having fold column might work, as it can be made mostly whitespace with proper `fillchars`. But I don't really see much value in using fold column in the first place.
- Fortunately, sign column is always at least two cells wide and signs are usually one cell wide. So showing lnum-signs-sep allows to automatically balance the whitespace.

The cost is indeed that signs are shown directly to the right of line numbers. However, for me this is a lower inconvenience problem, mostly because:
    - Signs are usually visibly differently highlighted than line numbers.
    - Signs can be adjusted to not be "that" left-aligned. For example, instead of left-aligned or centered line it can be right-aligned block (`🮈` or `▐`, see [this article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box-drawing_characters) for inspiration). Replacing signs with line number highlights for common signs (like for Git) is also a solution and what 'mini.diff' uses.

Luckily this is indeed customizable. Here is a [template to use as a starting point](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/1098976ddda3cf00f50c1dda5eef10ccf463d9eb/doc/mini-statuscolumn.txt#L208-L220).

> One issue I found so far is that if you open a floating terminal through `Snacks.terminal` then the statuscolumn isn't properly undimmed when it's closed. I was able to reproduce that using `Snacks.lazygit` and my own Tuxedo plugin when Snacks is installed.

@RVxLab, thanks! I can reproduce with the following config:

```lua
vim.g.mapleader = ' '
vim.o.signcolumn = 'yes'
vim.o.cursorline = true
vim.o.number = true

vim.pack.add({
  'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim',
  'https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim',
})

require('mini.statuscolumn').setup()
require('snacks').setup({ lazygit = { configure = false } })
vim.keymap.set('n', '<leader>g', function() Snacks.lazygit.open() end)
```

Likely 'snacks.nvim' blocks some autocommands from triggering. Because it works as expected with other floating windows and split terminals. I'll take a look.

> [@AGN907](https://github.com/AGN907), yes this is how it is supposed to look. The colored stuff is signs which are displayed to the right of line numbers. In the demo there are no signs (showing them would probably be a better idea), so the empty two cell column between line numbers and separator is for signs (since `signcolumn=yes` means to always show the column to reduce flickering).

I've updated the [demo](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/readmes/mini-statuscolumn.html#demo) to also include an example of how the statuscolumn looks with a present sign. Hope this make it clearer that this is an intended behavior.

> > One issue I found so far is that if you open a floating terminal through `Snacks.terminal` then the statuscolumn isn't properly undimmed when it's closed. I was able to reproduce that using `Snacks.lazygit` and my own Tuxedo plugin when Snacks is installed.
> ...
> Likely 'snacks.nvim' blocks some autocommands from triggering. Because it works as expected with other floating windows and split terminals. I'll take a look.

@RVxLab, this is indeed an issue with 'snacks.nvim' (the `snacks.terminal`, to be precise) blocking execution of relevant events during terminal closing. This is an example of a very common pitfall of not adding `nested = true` flag to an autocommand (otherwise it will block triggering other events).

The fix is rather simple (and makes dimming work as expected) and I'd expect to be done on 'snacks.terminal' side:

```diff
diff --git a/lua/snacks/terminal.lua b/lua/snacks/terminal.lua
index 132f0ef..a96d19b 100644
--- a/lua/snacks/terminal.lua
+++ b/lua/snacks/terminal.lua
@@ -143,7 +143,7 @@ function M.open(cmd, opts)
       end
       terminal:close()
       vim.cmd.checktime()
-    end, { buf = true })
+    end, { buf = true, nested = true })
   end
 
   terminal:on("ExitPre", function()
```

The quick search didn't show that this is a known issue or if there is a PR for this. So I'd encourage to address this upstream.

Awesome find, I was able to reproduce the fix locally. I raised it as an issue on the snacks.nvim repo.

Meanwhile as a workaround one can set `auto_close = false` when opening anything terminal related and manually setting `nested = true` on the `TermClose` event:

```lua
local snacks = require("snacks")

local terminal = snacks.lazygit.open({
    auto_close = false,
})

terminal:on("TermClose", function()
    if type(vim.v.event) == "table" and vim.v.event.status ~= 0 then
        snacks.notify.error(
            "Terminal exited with code " .. vim.v.event.status .. ".\nCheck for any errors."
        )
        return
    end
    terminal:close()
    vim.cmd.checktime()
end, { buf = true, nested = true })
```

I feel like the `MiniStatuscolumn.gen_content.main()` spec is a little bit clunky and mixes different concepts together, but I do like how concise it is. However, the main pain point for me is separating different types of signs into their own columns. [snacks.nvim/statuscolumn](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/main/docs/statuscolumn.md) allows to define `git` signs in a separate column. Here's how the [snacks.nvim](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/main/docs/statuscolumn.md) statuscolumn looks like: Also, is it possible to define multiple info fields per column and prioritize them in order? ``` format = "=l{fs}" ``` P.S. I know nothing about the `statuscolumn`, so it's not a strong opinion, just a vibe, srry 😅

Defining too many columns causes neovim to crash:

```lua
{ format = "ssssssssssss=lf", sep = " ▏" },
--          1234567890
```

Definitely not intended behavior, but a warning would still be better.

> I feel like the `MiniStatuscolumn.gen_content.main()` spec is a little bit clunky and mixes different concepts together, but I do like how concise it is.

Not sure how different are the concepts mixed. If you mean the "coordinate" and "info" fields, then this feels natural to me. At least as in how final spec array reads fairly naturally as what behavior it defines.
 
> However, the main pain point for me is separating different types of signs into their own columns. [snacks.nvim/statuscolumn](https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/main/docs/statuscolumn.md) allows to define `git` signs in a separate column.

Making possible to separate signs into dedicated column was my initial plan too. However, there is currently no good (performant and concise) way to achieve that because there is no mechanism to hook into when signs update. The approach of 'snacks.statuscolumn' is to force refresh every 50ms about the state of signs in visible buffers, and this doesn't feel right to me.

The most reasonable solution would be to use a dedicated event for when signs change, but that seems to be out of scope (neovim/neovim#32185).

So in the end I decided to go with the built-in "all in one" sign column.

> Also, is it possible to define multiple info fields per column and prioritize them in order?
> ...
> Defining too many columns causes neovim to crash:

Each section is meant to be placed only once. I don't see a reason to have the same content (and it *will* be the same content for the same letter in `format`) be displayed several times.

> Defining too many columns causes neovim to crash:
> 
> { format = "ssssssssssss=lf", sep = " ▏" },
> --          1234567890
> 
> Definitely not intended behavior, but a warning would still be better.

Although this is not intended to be supported, could not reproduce.

> Oh, try adding `vim.o.signcolumn = "yes"`. Not sure what's going on, but if neovim is crashing, that's not really a mini issue:

I did have this set originally when could not reproduce. There were two (double) columns displaying the same sign.

Even with repro setup could not reproduce initially, but only after several restarts. Yeah, this is likely an issue with Nightly (because 0.12.5 works). It would probably help if you narrow this down to a snippet without 'mini.statuscolumn' and report upstream.
Dimming doesn't interact well with `:set bg=light` (left window is focused): Other than that I'm quite happy with this plugin :)

> I just need to think of them more as rules or overrides. Since there are only two things used for filtering (`win` and `ltype`), ...

That's what [the docs say](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9d01f392b33fb2ba36fbc87fc0bf4453e63ffb0a/doc/mini-statuscolumn.txt#L203-L208). And there are [three "coordinate" fields](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9d01f392b33fb2ba36fbc87fc0bf4453e63ffb0a/doc/mini-statuscolumn.txt#L194-L201) used for filtering.

> Dimming doesn't interact well with `:set bg=light` (left window is focused):

@AlexApps99, I've finally taken a look at this. The only way I see this behavior is if there is no explicit colorscheme applied and 'background' is set *after* setting up 'mini.statuscolumn'. If yes, then this is an intended behavior because in this case the `MiniStatuscolumnDim` group is already defined and was not cleared. There doesn't seem to be a good way to tell if that definition came from 'mini.statuscolumn' (i.e. automatic dimming computation) or from a custom highlight group definition (i.e. manual adjustment). As not overriding custom definitions is a higher priority, nothing is done here to adjust after changing the background. This is the behavior of all default highlight groups which have color attributes computed instead of the whole group linking to some other one (or having attributes that don't need computation, like underline, etc.).

There are rather straightforward solutions for this on the user side, though:
- Set background flavor explicitly before setting up any plugins.
- Set color scheme explicitly before or after setting up any plugins. Like with `vim.cmd('colorscheme default')` in this particular case. With this approach changing the background flavor will resource the color scheme; which usually means clearing all highlight groups; which will make default groups recompute.
- Manually define `MiniStatuscolumnDim` highlight group.
Yep, I can confirm those conditions applied to my config. `vim.cmd.colorscheme` works a treat, thanks :)

Thank you for all the work on `mini.nvim`, it has been a joy to use thus far! One feedback I have for `mini.statuscolumn` is that it doesn't play very nicely with Neogit: Neogit uses the sign column to show the open/close status of different sections, which looks unnatural when combined with the column line from `mini.statuscolumn`. I don't expect that this can be easily fixed, so I totally understand if this is out of scope for `mini.statusline`.

> One feedback I have for `mini.statuscolumn` is that it doesn't play very nicely with Neogit:

Thanks for the feedback! To be perfectly honest, both screenshots look okay to me.

> Neogit uses the sign column to show the open/close status of different sections, which looks unnatural when combined with the column line from `mini.statuscolumn`. I don't expect that this can be easily fixed, so I totally understand if this is out of scope for `mini.statusline`.

Yeah, with default content disabling separator only in certain filetypes is not something that can be done by a single setting. The following seems to work:

```lua
-- Track filetype per buffer for performance. Can be skipped in favor of
-- a later `vim.bo[data.buf_id].filetype` in a `content.active`.
local buf_ft = {}
local track_ft = function(ev) buf_ft[ev.buf] = vim.bo[ev.buf].filetype end
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd({ 'BufCreate', 'FileType' }, { callback = track_ft })

-- Define which filetypes should not have separator shown. Here it is only
-- `lua`, for Neogit it will be something like `neogit` (check with
-- `:=vim.bo.filetype` when inside a Neogit buffer).
local nosep_ft = { lua = true }

-- Define a custom content, which will show separator in active window, but
-- not if it shows a buffer with a special filetype
local statuscolumn = require('mini.statuscolumn')
local spec = {
  { format = '=lfs', sep = ' ' },
  { ltype = 'virt', lnum = '•' },
  { ltype = 'wrap', lnum = '↳' },
  { win = 'active', sep = '▏' },
}
local content_sep = statuscolumn.gen_content.main(spec)
spec[4] = nil
local content_nosep = statuscolumn.gen_content.main(spec)

local active_sep, active_nosep = content_sep.active, content_nosep.active
local active = function(data) return (nosep_ft[buf_ft[data.buf_id]] and active_nosep or active_sep)(data) end

statuscolumn.setup({ content = { active = active, inactive = content_nosep.inactive } })
```

This can be trimmed with some performance cost (like checking `vim.bo[buf_id].filetype` on every draw multiple times).
Thank you! I will experiment with this.
